newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Nov 1.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Friday:
- The republic of Chechnya remains a part of Russia in name alone after Chechen rebels beat the Russian army two months ago.
- A kidnapping epidemic is frightening foreign investors in Mexico and giving the impression that parts of the country are slipping into chaos.
- The Justice Department is considering whether to get an independent counsel to probe into alleged wrong-doing by Democratic party fundraisers.
- Third-quarter, corporate results hint that earnings growth will be the smallest since profits fell in 1991.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton and his Republican rival Bob Dole embark on the last leg of their respective campaigns before presidential elections next week.
- The U.S. National Research Council did not find any convincing evidence that exposure to electric and magnetic fields from power lines and home appliances might be a health hazard.
